extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current students interested in journalism, communication, and media production (also alumni and industry partners)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview page for Carleton University's School of Journalism and Communication describing program aims, student outcomes, news, experiential opportunities (internships, fellowships, capstones), and faculty leadership. Intended to inform prospective/current students and stakeholders about curriculum goals and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism program outcome — produce compelling, impactful stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who complete our Journalism program will be equipped to produce compelling, impactful stories and lead the industry’s digital renaissance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioning of the Journalism program emphasizes both storytelling quality ('compelling, impactful stories') and leadership in digital transformation of the industry ('lead the industry’s digital renaissance'). No explicit scoring guidance; presented as program outcome/expectation for graduates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and Media Studies outcome — evaluate and shape media flows
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication and Media Studies students will be prepared to evaluate, manage, influence and shape the constant flow of images and information that are redefining all aspects of our lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames graduates' competency as critical/media management skills across image and information ecosystems; emphasizes active influence and shaping rather than passive analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Production and Design outcome — transform conversation and non-fiction narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Students in our Media Production and Design program will be at the forefront of transforming the ways in which we talk to each other and immerse ourselves in non-fiction narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program outcome stresses innovation in modes of communication and immersive non-fiction storytelling as core competencies for graduates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and career readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Our graduates are ideally positioned to apply their knowledge and expertise to be leaders in their careers and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit program metric: graduates should translate learned skills into leadership roles in professional and community contexts; supported by references to alumni network and long program history but no formal evaluation rubric provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capstone and showcased student projects as assessment/experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Production and Design capstone event showcases student projects; graduating students ... showed off their work in a remarkable capstone event, showcasing nine innovative student projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capstone projects function as a culminating, public demonstration of student learning and innovation; suggests practical, portfolio-style assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiential learning via internships, fellowships, and funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities listed include paid CBC internships supported by the McGuire fund, the Michener – L. Richard O’Hagan Fellowship for Journalism Education, Global Journalism Internships, CBC North Internship Program, and Emerging Reporter Funds to support student-produced journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes practical, often paid, experiential learning and external fellowships as core pathways for student development; examples include travel-fund support and paid placements. The page highlights these as program strengths rather than providing application selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized certificate outcomes (Indigenous journalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students in Carleton’s new Indigenous journalism certificate demonstrate their storytelling superpowers (noted via an in-person intensive course on audio journalism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates certificate-focused, intensive training (e.g., audio journalism) aimed at demonstrable storytelling skills in Indigenous journalism contexts; presented as a program success narrative rather than a scored rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty experience and industry engagement as program quality indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty profiles and news (e.g., Elly Alboim’s career as Ottawa Bureau Chief for CBC News and service with Earnscliffe Strategies; faculty appointments to expert panels) are presented as evidence of faculty expertise and industry connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program quality is partly justified by faculty professional experience, industry roles and external recognition; this functions as an implicit standard for program credibility and mentorship quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice to prospective applicants — engage with program resources
rubrics_metrics.description: To those of you thinking of joining us, please browse our website, write to us if you have questions, and visit us on campus to tour our facilities, meet with our faculty, and connect with our students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural guidance: active engagement (website review, contacting program heads, campus visits) is encouraged as part of applicant exploration; not a selection criterion but guidance for prospective students to assess fit and resources.
